item.title: Woman charged after shots fired into occupied home in Claiborne County - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
CLAIBORNE COUNTY – A woman has been charged after deputies responded to a report of shots fired into an occupied residence, according to the Claiborne County Sheriff’s Department.

Authorities said deputies were dispatched March 15 to a home on Woodvine Road after receiving a call about gunfire.

Upon arrival, occupants told deputies that TNeesha Edwards had discharged a firearm into the residence.

Following an investigation, Edwards was charged with shooting into a dwelling.

Officials said Edwards made an initial appearance in court, where Judge Odom set her bond at $20,000.

item.title: Two arrested on drug charges during Pearl River County patrol - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
PEARL RIVER COUNTY – Two individuals were arrested on drug-related charges earlier this month after being located by narcotics investigators in Pearl River County, according to the Pearl River County Sheriff’s Department.

Authorities said that on March 2, investigators with the department’s Narcotics Division were patrolling the area of Emmett Meitzler Road when they observed a man sitting near the intersection of Emmett Meitzler Road and Carey Meitzler Road.

Investigators identified the individual as Jace Phelps, who was wanted as part of “Operation County Sweep” on an outstanding warrant for the sale of narcotics. Phelps was taken into custody without incident.

During a search, deputies reported finding methamphetamine, a digital scale and marijuana in Phelps’ possession.

While on scene, investigators also observed a 2011 Infiniti arrive, driven by Elizabeth Levron. Deputies said Levron was also wanted as part of Operation County Sweep on an outstanding warrant for the sale of narcotics.

Levron was taken into custody, and a search of her vehicle allegedly revealed methamphetamine, drug paraphernalia and baggies, according to the sheriff’s department.

Both suspects were transported to the Pearl River County Correctional Facility.

item.title: Three taken into custody in shoplifting case at Guns-N-Gear - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
GLUCKSTADT – Three suspects were taken into custody Thursday after officers responded to a shoplifting call at a business in Gluckstadt, according to the Gluckstadt Police Department.

Police said officers were dispatched March 19 to Guns-N-Gear, located at 1716 Highway 51, after the store owner reported a shoplifting in progress.

Authorities said officers arrived within seconds and detained all three suspects before they were able to leave the store.

During the investigation, officers discovered a stolen firearm, police said.

One juvenile was transported to the Yazoo City Juvenile Detention Facility on a charge of conspiracy.

Police said Lamarcus Pate was also charged with conspiracy.

Mitchell Robinson is facing multiple charges, including shoplifting, conspiracy, possession of a stolen firearm and service of an active warrant for an additional possession of a stolen firearm charge.

Officials said Robinson and Pate are awaiting their initial appearance in Gluckstadt Municipal Court.

Police credited the patrol division’s quick response and follow-up investigation with helping resolve the case.

item.title: Spring Market of Jackson returns this weekend at Mississippi Trade Mart, includes CARA fundraiser - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
JACKSON — The Spring Market of Jackson is set to return this weekend, bringing shopping, local vendors and special events to the Mississippi Trade Mart.

The three-day event will take place March 20–22 and will feature a wide variety of vendors offering spring clothing, accessories and home décor, along with opportunities to support local businesses.

Show hours are scheduled for 9 a.m. to 8 p.m. Friday, 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. Saturday and 11 a.m. to 4 p.m. Sunday.

General admission tickets are $10, with a three-day pass available for $18. Specialty ticket options include a $20 “Friday Date Night” and a $20 “Saturday Muffins & Mimosas” experience.

During Friday night’s Date Night event, attendees will also have the opportunity to support Community Animal Rescue and Adoption (CARA). Organizers said “gold bags” will be available for purchase, with proceeds benefiting the organization.

Each bag, priced starting at $20, contains one to four $25 gift certificates to market vendors, offering attendees a chance to shop while supporting a local animal rescue.

Guests can also receive $1 off admission with a cash-only coupon at the door and register for door prizes, including a $250 “Shop the Show” grand prize.

Officials encourage families to attend, noting that children 12 and under receive free admission. The event will also feature free parking, a package check service, a photo booth and a variety of food options.

Organizers said the Spring Market of Jackson is designed to provide a fun, family-friendly shopping experience while supporting local businesses and community organizations.

More information and tickets are available at www.themarketshows.com .

item.title: Southaven police K9s receive protective vests through nonprofit donation - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
SOUTHAVEN — Two Southaven Police Department K9s have received bullet- and stab-protective vests through a donation from the nonprofit organization Vested Interest in K9s Inc., according to the department.

The department said K9s Raptor and Zargo were each outfitted with custom protective vests sponsored by the charity. The vests are embroidered with the message: “In memory of K9 Luca, DeSoto County, MS – EOW 2/21/24.”

Vested Interest in K9s Inc., founded in 2009, is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit that provides protective vests and other assistance to law enforcement dogs and related agencies across the United States.

According to the organization, the body armor is made in the United States, custom-fitted and certified by the National Institute of Justice. Since its founding, the nonprofit says it has provided more than 6,348 vests valued at $6.9 million to K9s in all 50 states.

The program is open to U.S. law enforcement dogs that are at least 20 months old, actively employed and certified with a law enforcement or related agency. K9s with expired vests are also eligible.

The organization said each vest is valued at $1,800, weighs an average of 4 to 5 pounds and includes a five-year warranty. A donation of $1,050 sponsors one vest.

More information about the organization, volunteer opportunities and donations is available at vik9s.org.

item.title: Quinton Tellis Trial Day 5: "Jay" takes the stand in afternoon testimony and tells a different story - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
MONROE, Louisiana — The man Quinton Tellis initially built his story of a debit card stolen from a dead girl around testified in Ouachita Parish Court Friday afternoon, and if his testimony is true, it debunks Tellis’s winding tales of the man named Jay.

Tellis is on trial in Monroe in the 2015 stabbing death of Ming Chen “Mandy” Hsiao, a Taiwanese national who had just finished graduate school in education at the University of Louisiana Monroe.

When investigators interviewed Tellis in the days after Hsiao was found dead, he told a story of a man named Jay that he had met and done a drug deal with. He said Jay gave him the debit card and told him to go get cash off of it at the ATM.

When Tellis was shown a lineup by investigators, he pointed to a city employee named Termar Key. This piqued their interest because they knew Key from the drug scene at the time. They had Tellis call him from the interview room and set up a time to meet, and they went out and brought him in off a traffic stop.

On Friday, Key took the stand for the prosecution. ADA Holly Jones entered his criminal history into the record so he could speak freely about the parts of the questioning that involved drugs.

Key testified that he met Tellis one day at the Chevron when Key had gotten off work and had his lawnmower on a trailer behind his truck. Tellis approached him and asked if he needed help cutting grass. Key had said he might be able to find something for him and gave him his number.

He said he had never met Tellis before that day. Tellis called him later and “he asked me if I smoke,” Key said, clarifying that he was talking about marijuana. Tellis asked him for “a sack” and Key met him behind Burger King and sold him $10 worth of marijuana.

After that, Tellis called him one more time, Key said, and it was the time he called him from the interview room. He said he’d never dealt with him again since then.

When police picked him up that day, Key said, they quickly told him they weren’t worried about the drugs, that this was about a homicide.

Jones walked him through the warrants that were served on his truck and his car, how police searched his wallet and took a DNA swab.

“You did everything they asked you to do, didn’t you?” she asked.

“Yes ma’am,” he said.

At the time, he didn’t even know Tellis’s name, he said, though he’s learned it since.

Jones asked him about his own name, and Key told her his nickname is “Lucky.” His middle name is “Laquan.”

“So your name is Termar Laquan Key?” she asked. He confirmed that was correct.

“Have you ever had another nickname?” she asked. “Have you ever met Mr. Tellis other than at Chevron and Burger King? Did you know someone named Kenny?”

The answer to all of those were no. The “Kenny” she referred to was the name Tellis gave when he alleged that Hsiao had a boyfriend who had bought crack from him. Police were very skeptical of Kenny’s existence because they felt Hsiao was unlikely to be dating a “crackhead.”

As Tellis’s story unfolded, the bank card seemed to have been shuffled back and forth between “Jay” and “Kenny,” and by the end of it, it was unclear who it was that allegedly gave Tellis the card.

“So you never knew a Kenny who was the boyfriend of an Asian girl?” Jones asked.

“No ma’am.”

“Did you ever go by the name ‘Jay?'”

“No ma’am.”

“Have you ever stolen a Chase bank card?” she pressed. “Did you ever instruct the defendant to take that bank card to the ATM in exchange for weed?”

No and no.

When Termar Keys left the courtroom, it felt like the ghost of the alleged “Jay” left with him.

That ended testimony for Friday, and for the immediate future. The trial was expected to have lasted only four days, but the prosecution still has several witnesses to call. Because of court scheduling, the judge and the attorneys floated some possible return dates, which could be as soon as April 1 or as far off as May 12. They are expected to come to an agreement next week on when to return.

Still expected to testify are Tellis’s ex-wife, Chakita Jackson, as well as some additional experts and some other storyline witnesses. The defense is calling one expert witness to dispute the prosecution’s cell phone data testimony.

Tellis remains in the custody of the Louisiana Department of Corrections in the meantime.

item.title: Quinton Tellis trial Day 5: Graphic autopsy photos appear to bolster torture claims - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
MONROE, Louisiana — As the prosecution submitted the autopsy photos during the testimony of forensic pathologist Dr. Frank Peretti in the murder trial of Quinton Tellis in the brutal stabbing death of Ming Chen Hsiao in 2015, the room was stone silent.

Reflected in the photos was a horrific death. There were 30 stab wounds, 27 of which were superficial, to the back the back of the head and neck, under the ears, and to the upper body. The other three, to the carotid and jugular on both the right and left side, would have been fatal, Peretti said.

Peretti also showed the judge where there were defense wounds to Hsiao’s hands, as she had tried to block herself from the attack. The advanced decomposition of 10 days in the August heat had rendered the 34-year-old Taiwanese national’s face unrecognizable and a stark contrast to the friendly, smiling face used by the media in stories and news reports.

The superficial wounds were between 1/4 and 1/2 inch deep, Peretti said, and they varied in length. Peretti testified that there was no way to tell which wounds were first, but the ones to the neck were the ones that had been fatal. He said once those stab wounds were administered, she would have died in less than three minutes.

On Thursday, witness Eric Hill told the court that Tellis had told him that “he stabbed a Chinese girl” for her bank card PIN number.

Peretti testified that based on the decomposition, it appeared that Hsiao had been dead for more than a week, and that a period of 10 days would make sense.

FOR MORE QUINTON TELLIS COVERAGE, CLICK HERE.

The prosecution holds that Tellis killed Hsiao in her Monroe apartment on July 29, 2015. She was found dead by neighbors and her landlord on August 8, 2015, which also happened to be the date of Tellis’s wedding to his wife at the time, Chakita Jackson.

Prior to Peretti’s testimony, the prosecution brought in Michelle Jackson, the deputy director of DNA at the North Louisiana Criminalistics Laboratory, to testify to what was found at the crime scene. Essentially, Michelle Jackson told the court that there was no DNA that could tie Tellis to the scene, but there was very little that could tie anyone but the victim to the scene.

There are multiple reasons that there might not be another identifiable DNA profile, she said. If a suspect had used barriers such as gloves, long sleeves, or a condom, there wouldn’t be any DNA.

The other possibility is that the advanced decomposition of Hsiao’s body would have decomposed outside DNA as well.

The blood found at the scene was all consistent with Hsiao’s except one swab from the bathroom that had two profiles — a male and a female — and neither of those profiles matched Hsiao’s or any of the other 14 people whose DNA was tested, including Tellis. Michelle Jackson testified that there’s no way to tell how long DNA has been there.

There was also evidence of male DNA in Hsaio’s rectal swab that didn’t match any of those who were tested, but Jackson said it was impossible to tell if it was from skin, blood, or semen cells. In addition, it was a partial profile and there was no way to know how long it had been there. She also did not know if the medical examiner had taken the swab from the inside or outside of the rectum.

Tellis is the main suspect in the 2014 Jessica Chambers burning death in Panola County, Mississippi. There was very little DNA in that case as well, but a DNA profile found on her car keys matched Tellis’s familial DNA.

Court let out for lunch at noon and will be back for more testimony from prosecution witnesses at 1:30 p.m.

item.title: Kemper County man arrested on 20 child pornography charges - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
KEMPER COUNTY – A Kemper County man was arrested Thursday after a joint investigation by the Kemper County Sheriff’s Office and the FBI into the alleged download of child pornography from the dark web.

According to the Kemper County Sheriff’s Office, investigators and federal agents spent several weeks investigating an individual identified through intelligence sources as allegedly downloading large amounts of child pornographic material.

Officials said the investigation found the suspect had accumulated several hundred gigabytes of the material.

At about 6 a.m. on March 19, the Kemper County Sheriff’s Office Special Response Team executed a search warrant and arrest warrant at a residence at 71 Parsonage Road in the Preston community.

Authorities said Timothy Walker was taken into custody without incident and charged with 20 counts of possession of child pornography.

Walker’s bond was set at $250,000 per count, for a total of $5 million, according to the sheriff’s office.

Sheriff’s officials said the case remains part of ongoing efforts to investigate and prosecute crimes involving the exploitation of children.

All suspects are presumed innocent until proven guilty.

item.title: Hattiesburg firefighters respond to house fire on North 35th Avenue - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
HATTIESBURG — The Hattiesburg Fire Department responded to a residential structure fire late Friday morning in the city.

Fire crews were dispatched around 11 a.m. on March 20 to the 500 block of North 35th Avenue after a Hattiesburg Police officer reported seeing smoke coming from a home and alerted dispatch.

Officials said firefighters arrived to find heavy smoke coming from the residence and immediately began suppression efforts while searching the structure.

No occupants were found inside the home.

Crews were able to bring the fire under control quickly due to what officials described as an aggressive initial response.

Units responding to the scene included Engines 4, 6 and 9, Ladders 1 and 6, and Tower 8.

The cause of the fire remains under investigation. No additional information has been released.

item.title: Greenville man sentenced to additional prison time for drug trafficking - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
GREENVILLE – A Greenville man has been sentenced in federal court for drug trafficking, according to the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Northern District of Mississippi.

Michael Lawrence Hunt, 45, previously pleaded guilty to possession of methamphetamine with intent to distribute.

According to court documents, Greenville police discovered more than 55 methamphetamine pills and other illegal substances during a traffic stop on Sept. 11, 2024. Authorities said Hunt had a prior felony conviction at the time of the offense.

Senior U.S. District Judge Michael P. Mills sentenced Hunt to 45 months in prison, followed by three years of supervised release. Hunt was remanded to the custody of the U.S. Marshals after sentencing.

The case was investigated by the Greenville Police Department and the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives.

U.S. Attorney Scott Leary said drug trafficking continues to harm communities across the state.

“Meth addiction is one of the hardest addictions to overcome, often resulting in destroyed lives and families,” Leary said. “Through continued diligence, our communities must be reclaimed for the hard-working Mississippians that live there.”

ATF Special Agent in Charge Joshua Jackson said the agency will continue working with local and federal partners to target repeat offenders and reduce drug-related crime.

Greenville Police Chief Marcus R. Turner also thanked the agencies involved, saying the department will continue using all available resources to pursue those who violate the law.

The case is part of Project Safe Neighborhoods, a federal initiative aimed at reducing violent crime and improving public safety through coordinated law enforcement efforts.

item.title: Three charged after contraband introduced into Pearl River County jail - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
PEARL RIVER COUNTY – Three people have been charged following an investigation into contraband brought into the Pearl River County Correctional Facility during inmate visitation, according to the Pearl River County Sheriff’s Department.

Narcotics investigators responded to the facility on Feb. 17 after receiving reports that contraband had been introduced during visitation.

Following the visit, correctional officers searched inmates and found Andrew Sellers, 23, in possession of contraband, according to the Sheriff’s Department.

Investigators determined that another inmate, Pharoah Lyons, 53, was involved in bringing the contraband into the facility, along with a visitor, Kirby Haynes, 41, of Waveland.

Sellers and Lyons were each charged with introduction of contraband into a correctional facility. A warrant was issued for Haynes’ arrest.

On March 4, Haynes was arrested by the Waveland Police Department and transported to the Pearl River County Correctional Facility, where she was also charged with introduction of contraband into a correctional facility.

Sheriff David Allison praised correctional officers for their efforts in detecting and preventing contraband from entering the facility.

item.title: Tellis trial Day 4: "You better put this on someone else or I'll F you up." - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
MONROE, Louisiana — Eric Hill barely looked in Quinton Tellis’s direction as he told a tale of homicide, lies and intimidation.

After hearing from Mandy Hsiao’s landlord and a friend who gave her a ride to the bank on the last day she was alive, ADA Holly Jones called Hill, who could be considered the prosecution’s star witness, to the stand in Ouachita Parish where Tellis is on trial in Hsiao’s 2015 stabbing death. Tellis, who is from Mississippi, is also the main suspect in the 2014 death of Jessica Chambers in Courtland.

Hill is the cousin of Tellis’s ex-wife, Chakita Jackson. Their wedding was held on the day Hsiao’s body was found.

A few days after the wedding, Hill testified, Tellis told Hill about how he had gone into “a Chinese lady’s” house and taken her into her bedroom and stabbed her until she gave him her Chase debit card pin number. He said he had met Hsiao while fishing, and told Hill he needed to find another Asian woman who could go withdraw the money using Hsiao’s ID. He allegedly told Hill to do it for him, but Hill refused. He said he knew that if he used a homicide victim’s card, the investigation would eventually come around to him.

Hill testified that he didn’t tell anyone about that conversation because he was afraid of what Tellis might do to him or to Jackson.

Throughout his testimony, Hill was calm and resolute. He showed no visible emotion as he admitted to his lies and implicated the man he said frightened him enough to tell them.

When Tellis was arrested after detectives linked him to the debit card, Hill testified, someone he is fairly certain was Tellis called him on a three-way call from jail. There is no recording of the call, and Jones said that three-way calls are often used along with other inmate’s access numbers to get around the system that tracks calls to and from a particular inmate.

On that call, Hill testified, Tellis allegedly told him, “You better put this on someone else or I’ll f— you up.”

“It made me feel threatened and scared for my life,” Hill said. “He already told me what he did to the lady. I was afraid for my life and Chakita’s.”

Hill said he called Monroe Police Department and told them a man named Curtis Lemons had committed the crime, and he told them how it was done. At that point, none of those details were available in the news.

Jones asked him how he decided on Lemons as his target. Hill said that he was “the last person I had a problem with.” In Hill’s original story, it was Lemons who had originally taken Hsiao’s ID and blue Chase bank card. But he also told them Lemons had given the card to Tellis.

“Why did you tell them Tellis had it?” Jones asked.

“I don’t know,” Hill said.

But soon the investigation did come back to him, Hill testified, when authorities found that Lemons had nothing to do with the crime. In March 2016, Hill was arrested and told he would be charged with accessory after the fact to murder. At that point, he confessed that the story he had told them before was true, but that the man who allegedly killed Hsiao had been Tellis, not Lemons.

Tellis went on to plead guilty to using Hsiao’s debit card. A few years later, both men were in the Department of Corrections and they were housed in the same pod, Hill testified. He said it was his understanding that they never should have had that living arrangement.

Hill said he wrote an affidavit during that time that recanted his testimony against Tellis. He said in the document that the only details he knew were the ones he’d seen in the news. On that affidavit were two sets of handwriting: Hill’s and Tellis’s.

“He told me I needed to sign the affidavit and make it right or he would do something to me,” Hill said. He testified that he didn’t even see any coverage from the time after the homicide until much later.

“Were you afraid for your safety?” Jones asked.

“Yes ma’am,” Hill testified.

“Are you concerned today about your safety?” she asked.

“Yes ma’am,” he said.

On cross examination, defense attorney Randall Donald hammered on the fact that Hill had made three previous statements, and two were lies. He walked up to the stand and had Hill read the affidavit with him, pointing out the phrase, “Under penalty of perjury” and others that were inserted to stress the importance of telling the truth.

Hill stood firm that he did, in fact, lie, but he did it because he was afraid of Tellis.

Donald asked him again about whether he was sure the phone call came from Tellis, and Hill said he was fairly certain. He said to Donald and on redirect that it sounded like Tellis. At that point, he testified, he had known Tellis for a year and a half and had more conversations than he could count with him.

When Donald pressed on the perjury issue again, Hill said, “Quinton Tellis told me if I didn’t sign it, something would happen to me. There was nowhere to run, nowhere to hide, and we were in a jail where nobody cared about my safety or anybody else’s.”

Hill was asked by the defense about his previous convictions, and he has some drug charges, a simple robbery and a simple burglary, which means no weapons were involved.

Before lunch, Detective Duane Cookson returned to the stand as the prosecution showed more of Tellis’s interview videos. They are the same ones that were shown on Monday to the judge. They were shown to him in their entirety, court officials said, in order to show him that Tellis was not in any way coerced or intimidated by the police.

Court resumes at 1:30 p.m.

item.title: Suspect shot after allegedly trying to hit Harrison County deputy with vehicle - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
GULFPORT – The Mississippi Bureau of Investigation is investigating an officer-involved shooting involving the Harrison County Sheriff’s Office that occurred March 19 near Five Oaks Drive.

According to authorities, deputies responded to a call regarding a domestic dispute and located a vehicle believed to be involved.

Officials said as a deputy approached, the subject allegedly attempted to strike the deputy with the vehicle. The deputy then discharged his weapon, striking the subject.

The subject was transported to a nearby hospital. The deputy was not seriously injured, and no other injuries were reported.

The Mississippi Bureau of Investigation is assessing the incident and gathering evidence. Once the investigation is complete, findings will be turned over to the Mississippi Attorney General’s Office.

Officials said the information released is preliminary and subject to change. Additional details may be released at a later time.

item.title: Meridian Child on Bicycle Critically Injured After Being Struck by Car - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Cash Matlock
item.description:
MERIDIAN – A young child was critically injured Wednesday evening after being struck by a vehicle while riding a bicycle in Meridian, authorities said.

Officers with the Meridian Police Department responded to the scene around 5:30 p.m. in the 1400 block of 19th Street, according to a statement from the city.

Upon arrival, officers determined that the child had been hit by a vehicle. The child was airlifted to a hospital in Jackson and remains in critical condition, officials said.

Assistant Police Chief Dareall Thompson asked the community for support as the situation unfolds.

“We ask our community to lift this child and their family up in prayer during this difficult time,” Thompson said. “We also ask that you keep the officers who responded in your prayers as well.”

Mayor Percy Bland also expressed gratitude for first responders and called for unity.

“I am grateful for the quick and professional response of our Meridian Police Department and first responders,” Bland said. “In moments like this, we come together as a community. Please join me in keeping this child, the family, and everyone involved in your prayers.”

The incident remains under investigation by the department’s Traffic Enforcement Division. Authorities said additional details will be released as they become available.

No further information, including the child’s identity or the circumstances leading to the crash, has been released.

item.title: Hinds County unveils Fallen Deputies & Jailers Monument honoring those who made ultimate sacrifice - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
HINDS COUNTY – The Hinds County Sheriff’s Office unveiled a new monument Thursday honoring deputies and jailers who died in the line of duty.

According to Sheriff Tyree Jones, the Fallen Deputies & Jailers Monument serves as a permanent tribute to the men and women who made the ultimate sacrifice while serving the community.

“This memorial stands as a lasting reminder that while their watch has ended, their legacy lives on,” Jones said in a statement. “Every visitor who walks these grounds will know that heroes served here and that their sacrifice will never be forgotten.”

Jones expressed gratitude to the families of the fallen, recognizing their strength and continued dedication to honoring their loved ones.

The sheriff also thanked Hinds County Board of Supervisors President Robert Graham, Vice President Wanda Evers and other board members for their role in supporting the project, as well as county leaders, law enforcement agencies and community members who attended the unveiling.

Members of the Hinds County Sheriff’s Office, the Jackson Police Department and other partnering agencies were present for the ceremony, along with clergy, elected officials and community partners.

Jones also recognized Felicia Tripp for her work in coordinating the ceremony.

Sheriff Tyree Jones stated,

“Today was a powerful reminder of duty, sacrifice, and the enduring bond of the law enforcement family.

item.title: Hernando Police Department honors fallen K-9 Luna - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
HERNANDO – The Hernando Police Department is mourning the loss of K-9 Luna, a police dog remembered for her service, loyalty and dedication to the community.

In a statement shared on social media, the department described Luna as more than just a police dog, calling her a “loyal partner, a brave protector, and a silent hero who stood on the front lines without hesitation.”

Officials said Luna played a vital role in helping keep both the community and fellow officers safe through her work.

“Your courage helped keep your community and your fellow officers safe, and your dedication will never be forgotten,” the department said.

The department also expressed gratitude for Luna’s service and the bond she shared with those she worked alongside.

“Thank you for your service, your loyalty, and the love you gave so freely. You did your job with honor, and you did it well,” the post read.

Luna’s passing marks the loss of a valued member of the department and a trusted partner in law enforcement.

Gonzales suffered fatal injuries and was pronounced dead at the scene.

The crash remains under investigation by the Mississippi Highway Patrol.

item.title: 18-year-old found shot to death inside Jackson apartment - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
JACKSON – An 18-year-old man lost his life after a shooting at a Jackson apartment complex last night.

According to Police Chief Tyree Jones, officers were called to Rebelwood apartments at 5:15 p.m.

Sheriff Jones said officers found a black male who had been shot multiple times and was pronounced deceased at the scene.

There are no suspects right now and officer detained several witnesses for questioning.

If you know anything, please contact Jackson police or Crimestoppers.

In a press conference at the scene, Sheriff Jones described the scene as “concerning” due to the magnitude of shell casings recovered at the scene.

He talked about the importance of conflict resolution without firearms.

“We ask people to not introduce guns to conflict resolution. If you have an issue or conflict, find a better way to solve an issue then involving guns into conflict”.

This is the capital city’s 15th homicide of 2026.

item.title: U.S. Marshals capture fugitive wanted in Winston County shooting - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
WINSTON COUNTY – A man wanted in connection with a shooting in Winston County and the attempted shooting of a law enforcement officer has been captured, according to the U.S. Marshals Service.

Bobby White Jr., 45, was arrested March 17 in Ackerman following a fugitive investigation led by the U.S. Marshals Service. item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
CARROLL COUNTY – Two men have been charged after deputies recovered a vehicle stolen from a senior citizen earlier this week, according to Carroll County officials.

Authorities said the Carroll County Emergency Operations Center received a call Monday morning, March 16, from a senior citizen who discovered her only mode of transportation had been stolen. Deputies were dispatched to a residence near the Greenwood Leflore Airport.

We don’t rest until those who prey on them are held accountable.”

Walker also credited the cooperation between agencies for the quick recovery of the vehicle.

item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
PIKE COUNTY – The Pike County Sheriff’s Office has added a new member to assist in the fight against online child exploitation through its partnership with the Mississippi Internet Crimes Against Children Task Force, according to Sheriff Bryant “Wally” Jones.

Officials said Intelligence Analyst Aaron Adams joined the ICAC Task Force as an affiliate member on Monday, March 16.

The ICAC Unit, operated by the Mississippi Attorney General’s Office, is responsible for investigating online child exploitation cases across the state.

Adams joins Lt. Det. Javonda Shanks of the Pike County Sheriff’s Office, who has served as an affiliate member of the task force since 2024. Former Pike County Sheriff’s Office detectives Matthew Travis and Max Adams also serve as full-time members of the ICAC Task Force under the Attorney General’s Office.

Sheriff Jones said the addition strengthens the county’s ongoing efforts to protect children and support statewide investigations.

“I’m proud of Aaron and all of the ICAC members who help keep our communities safe from child predators,” Jones said. “He will be a great addition to the unit and brings a lot of talent to the table. We will continue to partner with the Mississippi Attorney General and the ICAC Unit for years to come.”

The sheriff’s office said the partnership reflects its continued commitment to combating online child exploitation and enhancing public safety.

item.title: Natchez to host program on Indigenous language revitalization, annual powwow later this month - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
NATCHEZ – A public program highlighting the history and revitalization of the Indigenous Natchez language will be held later this month, followed by the city’s annual Natchez Powwow, according to event organizers.

The language program is scheduled for Wednesday, March 26, at 6 p.m. at the Grand Village of the Natchez Indians. The event will feature Dr. Geoffrey Kimball, author of Natchez Analytical Dictionary, who will discuss the last fluent speakers of the Natchez language and early 20th-century efforts to document it.

Dr. Keith Cunningham will also speak about how the newly published dictionary is being used to help descendants of the Natchez people develop educational tools aimed at reviving the language.

Relatives of the last fluent speakers from the Sam family are expected to attend and share their genealogy and ongoing preservation efforts.

Following the program, attendees will have the opportunity to meet Kimball during a book signing. Copies of the dictionary will be available for purchase. The event is free and open to the public, and refreshments will be provided.

“The Natchez language is an important part of the history of this region,” said Roscoe Barnes, cultural heritage and tourism manager for Visit Natchez. “Programs like this allow residents and visitors to learn more about the people and stories connected to Natchez while supporting efforts to document and revitalize the language for future generations.”

Later in the week, the Natchez Powwow will take place March 28–29 on the Natchez Bluff at 319 N. Broadway St. The annual event will feature Native American dancers, singers, artisans and vendors from across the region.

Organizers said the family-friendly event will include traditional dance exhibitions, music, arts and crafts, and food vendors. Admission is free.

“This is a wholesome family event that provides good entertainment and a celebration of Native American culture in a safe environment,” said Natchez Powwow Chairman Dr. Chuck Borum. “We invite everyone to come enjoy themselves.”

Oscar-nominated songwriter Scott George, known for “Wahzhazhe (A Song for My People)” from Killers of the Flower Moon, is expected to participate in this year’s powwow, along with Eddie Yellowfish, who will serve as head singer of the Southern Drum.

Organizers encourage attendees to bring lawn chairs for seating.

For more information, visit natchezpowwow.com.

item.title: Missing Covington County man found dead in Mississippi River after weeks long search - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
ADAMS COUNTY – The Adams County Sheriff’s Office says a missing man who was originally reported out of Covington County has been found dead after an extensive multi-agency search.

According to the sheriff’s office, Cornelius Elijah Allen, 31, was located deceased in the Mississippi River near the Hydro Plant on Highway 15 in Louisiana, about an hour from Vidalia.

Authorities said Allen was identified through personal identification found on his body. The Natchez Police Department, which has been leading the investigation, confirmed the discovery. Family members have been notified.

Allen was originally reported missing Feb. 25, 2026.

UPDATE: Missing man’s vehicle found abandoned near Natchez riverfront

His body was found after weeks of coordinated search efforts involving the Adams County Search and Rescue Team, the Mississippi Department of Wildlife, Fisheries and Parks, the Adams County Sheriff’s Office, the Natchez Police Department and the Concordia Parish Sheriff’s Office.

Sheriff Travis Patten and the Adams County Sheriff’s Office thanked the agencies, volunteers and community members who assisted in the search.

“Our thoughts and prayers are with Mr. Allen’s family during this incredibly difficult time,” Patten said. “We ask the community to continue to lift them up in prayer as they seek comfort and closure.”

The Adams County Sheriff’s Office said it will continue assisting the Natchez Police Department and partner agencies as the investigation continues.

item.title: Jackson State to host national teacher recruitment fair amid ongoing educator shortage - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
JACKSON – Jackson State University will host a national teacher recruitment fair this week as part of efforts to address ongoing educator shortages in Mississippi and across the country, according to a university press release.

The JSU Career Services Center will hold the 2026 Teacher Recruitment Fair on Thursday, March 19, from 9 a.m. to 12:30 p.m. in the Terry L. Woodard Ballroom on the third floor of the Student Center. The event is open to all majors and alumni, with opportunities for placement in K-12 classrooms.

“The Career Services Center has a long collaborative history with hosting this event for our education majors,” said Lashanda W. Jordan, executive director of JSU Career and Student Services. “We believe this event is important in assisting our students with launching their careers in the field of education.”

University officials said approximately 55 school districts from across the country are expected to participate, along with organizations such as Black Men Teach and Teachers Like Me, which focus on recruiting and supporting educators.

Jordan said the event allows Jackson State to connect its graduates with districts seeking qualified teachers and to highlight the university’s education programs on a national level.

The recruitment effort comes as Mississippi continues to face a significant teacher shortage. According to the Mississippi Department of Education, the state reported more than 6,000 vacancies for teachers, administrators and support staff based on a survey conducted between August and November 2025.

Officials have cited low pay, burnout and limited benefits as contributing factors. The largest shortages are in math, science and special education.

State lawmakers are currently working to reconcile competing proposals for teacher pay raises. The Mississippi Senate has approved a plan that would provide a $6,000 raise for teachers and an additional $3,000 for special education teachers, while the House has passed a plan offering a $5,000 raise phased in over three years.

Nationwide, a report from the Learning Policy Institute found nearly 46,000 unfilled teaching positions across 31 states and the District of Columbia.

University officials said the recruitment fair is an opportunity to help fill gaps while positioning Jackson State as a leading source of educators in Mississippi and beyond.

“The JSU Teacher Recruitment Day provides us the opportunity to showcase our talented students and ensure school districts across not only the state of Mississippi but the country know that our program is top-notch,” Jordan said.

item.title: "He gave me the creeps": Victim's neighbor testifies about meeting Tellis - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
MONROE, Louisiana — Katelyn Hearn remembers the day that she met the man she identified on Wednesday as Quinton Tellis, telling the court that “he creeped me out” enough that she went inside and locked the door.

Hearn testified on Day 3 of the murder trial of Tellis in the 2015 death of Ming Chen “Mandy” Hsiao in Monroe, Louisiana. Tellis, who remains the main suspect in the 2014 burning death of Jessica Chambers in Courtland, Mississippi, is alleged to have killed Hsiao less than 10 months after Chambers’ death.

Prosecutors used Hearn’s testimony to help draw out a timeline of when Tellis was at Hsiao’s apartment in the days leading up to her death.

Hearn said Hsiao had visitors from time to time, including a woman in a gold vehicle. But she had only seen the black Impala registered to Tellis’s then-fiancee Chakita Jackson within the week of Hsiao’s death. The first time she saw it, she told the court, was on July 27, 2015.

READ: Tellis trial, Day 1: Interview videos

She had been asleep, Hearn testified, when she heard someone knock on the door, and then heard footsteps retreating down the metal stairs outside her upstairs apartment. Thinking it was a package being delivered, she went to the door, where she found a child. Hearn said the child asked her, “Do you know where that white lady that lives downstairs is?”

Hearn told him no, then looked down the stairs to see an adult man standing by Hsiao’s bike and a young teenager standing by the Impala. The man she identified in court as Tellis struck up a conversation, asking her if she knew where Hsiao was. He ended up asking her,”Do you have a baby inside?”

The question was strange, Hearn thought, and she testified that “red flags went up.” She told the judge that she has an almost photographic memory, and it’s heightened when she has an extreme reaction to things. She testified that the fear that she felt sharpened her memory of Tellis, particularly his face. When she identified him in a photo lineup after Hsiao’s body was found, she remembered him clearly.

The black car would come back twice more that day, once after Hsiao came home, and then again that evening. On the second visit, she didn’t see Tellis, but she saw the two children from before playing in the yard. Given that she had been afraid the last time he was there, Hearn called her boyfriend and asked him to come home for lunch. When he left, Hearn asked him to get the license plate of the black Impala. She said she often gets the license numbers of strange vehicles.
